# pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster (Resource)

A managed Kubernetes cluster. Every node, control and worker, is a VM of node_plan in your account and is billed as one; there is no separate control-plane fee. Storage used by persistent volume claims (volume_storage_gb) is billed with the nodes' disks. workers, autoscaling and api_allowed_cidrs change in place with one PATCH; kubernetes_version_id changes in place to one of available_upgrade_ids (upgrade, never down); node_plan changes in place by moving every node to the new plan; endpoint_access changes in place. cni_plugin, pod_cidr and service_cidr are fixed when an appliance cluster is created, so changing them replaces it. Set either workers (a fixed count) or autoscaling (a range the cluster autoscaler moves the count within), not both. Changing name, zone_id, subnet_id or control_nodes replaces the cluster. A cluster that does not fit your account's limits fails with PROVISIONING_LIMIT_EXCEEDED before anything is created. Destroying it stops it at once and its nodes, disks and persistent volumes are destroyed 12 hours later. Its subnet stays in use until the nodes are removed in the background, so a pantechdynamics_subnet destroyed in the same run waits for that.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A cluster in a VPC subnet whose workers the cluster autoscaler keeps between
# 2 and 5, with its API server reachable only from an office range, and its
# kubeconfig written to a local file for kubectl.

resource "pantechdynamics_network" "main" {
  name = "main"
  cidr = "10.0.0.0/16"
}

# In a VPC zone the nodes go in a subnet. In a standard zone (af-abj-1) leave
# subnet_id out.
resource "pantechdynamics_subnet" "k8s" {
  network_id = pantechdynamics_network.main.id
  name       = "k8s"
  cidr       = "10.0.1.0/24"
}

# Firewall rules are stateless: the nodes need outbound traffic to pull images.
resource "pantechdynamics_firewall_rule" "k8s_egress" {
  subnet_id = pantechdynamics_subnet.k8s.id
  number    = 200
  direction = "egress"
  protocol  = "all"
  cidr      = "0.0.0.0/0"
}

# The versions offered in the network's zone, newest first.
data "pantechdynamics_kubernetes_versions" "zone" {
  zone_id = pantechdynamics_network.main.zone
}

locals {
  newest_version = [for v in data.pantechdynamics_kubernetes_versions.zone.versions : v if v.status == "available"][0]
}

resource "pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster" "prod" {
  name                  = "prod"
  zone_id               = pantechdynamics_network.main.zone
  subnet_id             = pantechdynamics_subnet.k8s.id
  kubernetes_version_id = local.newest_version.id

  # Every node, control and worker, is a VM of this plan and is billed as one.
  # It needs at least the version's min_cpu and min_memory_mb.
  node_plan = "s-2vcpu-4gb"

  # 1 (the default), or 3 where the zone is in ha_zone_ids. Changing it, the
  # name, zone or subnet replaces the cluster. A new node_plan changes in
  # place: every node is replaced, one at a time, by one of the new plan.
  control_nodes = 1

  # The pod network: flannel (default), wireguard (encrypted between nodes) or
  # calico (network policies). The ranges default to 10.42.0.0/16 and
  # 10.43.0.0/16. Changes rebuild the pod network in place; pods restart.
  cni_plugin = "calico"
  # pod_cidr     = "10.42.0.0/16"
  # service_cidr = "10.43.0.0/16"

  # Where the API server can be reached from: private (the default, only
  # inside the cluster's network), public or dual. public and dual hold a
  # public address billed as a VPC public IP. Changes in place.
  endpoint_access = "public"

  # The autoscaler adds and removes workers between min_workers and max_workers
  # as pods need them. The cluster starts at min_workers. Workers are billed as
  # VMs of node_plan while they run, and credit and account limits are checked
  # for max_workers. Changes in place. Leave workers out while autoscaling is
  # enabled: the autoscaler owns the count, which is reported in workers.
  autoscaling = {
    enabled     = true
    min_workers = 2
    max_workers = 5
  }

  # For a fixed count instead, remove autoscaling and set workers (1 to 10),
  # which changes in place (scale):
  # workers = 2

  # VPC zone only: the addresses allowed to reach the API server, at most 20
  # IPv4 CIDRs. Leave it out (or set []) to allow any address. Changes in place.
  api_allowed_cidrs = ["203.0.113.0/24"]

  # To upgrade, set kubernetes_version_id to one of available_upgrade_ids: the
  # next patch or minor version, never down.

  timeouts = {
    create = "60m"
    update = "60m"
    delete = "20m"
  }

  depends_on = [pantechdynamics_firewall_rule.k8s_egress]
}

# The kubeconfig is a cluster-admin credential. It is also in the Terraform
# state, so keep the state somewhere private.
resource "local_sensitive_file" "kubeconfig" {
  content         = pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.kube_config
  filename        = "${path.module}/kubeconfig-prod.yaml"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

output "kubernetes_version" {
  value = pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.kubernetes_version
}

# The API server's URL, and the storage persistent volume claims use (billed
# with the nodes' disks).
output "endpoint" {
  value = pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.endpoint
}

output "volume_storage_gb" {
  value = pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.volume_storage_gb
}

output "kubeconfig" {
  value     = pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod.kube_config
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `kubernetes_version_id` (String) Id of the Kubernetes version, starting with k8sv_, from the pantechdynamics_kubernetes_versions data source in zone_id. Changes in place by upgrading the cluster, which must be running: the new id must be one of available_upgrade_ids (the next patch or the next minor version). Upgrades never go down and never happen on their own.
- `name` (String) Name of the cluster: 1 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen. Unique in the organization. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `node_plan` (String) Slug of the plan every node uses, from the pantechdynamics_plans data source. It needs at least the version's min_cpu and min_memory_mb. Each node is billed as a VM of this plan. Changes in place: every node, control and worker, is replaced one at a time with a node of the new plan, and the cluster must be running. The API reports the plan only by id (node_plan_id), so a change made outside Terraform is not detected, and after an import this holds no value and setting it changes nothing.
- `zone_id` (String) Zone to create the cluster in, for example "af-abj-2" (a VPC zone, which needs subnet_id) or "af-abj-1" (a standard zone, which takes no subnet_id). The pantechdynamics_kubernetes_versions data source lists the versions per zone. Changing it replaces the cluster.

### Optional

- `api_allowed_cidrs` (Set of String) VPC zone only (needs subnet_id): the source addresses allowed to reach the API server, as at most 20 IPv4 CIDRs, for example ["203.0.113.0/24"]. Empty (the default) allows any address. Changes in place: the set is the whole list, and removing it allows any address again.
- `autoscaling` (Attributes) The cluster autoscaler, which adds and removes workers between min_workers and max_workers as pods need them. Workers are billed as VMs of node_plan while they run, and your credit and account limits are checked for max_workers. The cluster starts at min_workers. Changes in place. Removing it (or setting enabled = false) turns the autoscaler off and needs workers set: the count it lands on. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--autoscaling))
- `cni_plugin` (String) The pod network plugin: "flannel" (the default), "wireguard" (flannel with traffic between nodes encrypted) or "calico" (network policies). Fixed when an appliance cluster is created: changing it replaces the cluster.
- `control_nodes` (Number) Control plane nodes: 1 (the default), or 3 for a highly available control plane where the zone offers one (see ha_zone_ids on the pantechdynamics_kubernetes_versions data source). Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `endpoint_access` (String) Where the API server can be reached from: "private" (the default, only from inside the cluster's network), "public" (from the internet, limited by api_allowed_cidrs) or "dual" (both). public and dual give the API server a public address of its own (public_ip, public_port), billed as a VPC public IP for every hour it is held, and open its port on the subnet to api_allowed_cidrs (or any address). Changes in place; a change to public or dual finishes once the public address is routed.
- `pod_cidr` (String) The pods' IPv4 address range. Left unset, the platform picks the first of 10.42.0.0/16, 10.244.0.0/16, 172.20.0.0/16 and 192.168.0.0/17 that does not overlap the cluster's VPC network, subnet or service_cidr. A range that overlaps them is refused with KUBERNETES_POD_CIDR_OVERLAP. Fixed when an appliance cluster is created: changing it replaces the cluster.
- `service_cidr` (String) The services' IPv4 address range. Left unset, the platform picks the first of 10.43.0.0/16, 10.96.0.0/16, 172.21.0.0/16 and 192.168.128.0/17 that does not overlap the cluster's VPC network, subnet or pod_cidr. A range that overlaps them is refused with KUBERNETES_SERVICE_CIDR_OVERLAP. Fixed when an appliance cluster is created: changing it replaces the cluster.
- `subnet_id` (String) Id of the subnet the nodes go in, from pantechdynamics_subnet. Required in a VPC zone, and must be omitted in a standard zone. Changing it replaces the cluster.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `workers` (Number) A fixed number of worker nodes, 1 to 10. Required unless autoscaling is enabled, and must not be set while it is: the autoscaler then owns the count, which is reported here and never causes a diff. Changes in place by scaling the cluster, which must be running. Added workers are billed as VMs of node_plan. To go from autoscaling back to a fixed count, remove autoscaling and set workers.

### Read-Only

- `available_upgrade_ids` (List of String) Ids of the Kubernetes versions the cluster can be upgraded to now, the values kubernetes_version_id may change to.
- `created_at` (String) When the cluster was created, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `endpoint` (String) The API server's URL, once the cluster has one. Null until then. The kubeconfig points kubectl at it.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the cluster, starting with k8s_.
- `in_sync` (Boolean) False while a scale or upgrade has not finished.
- `kind` (String) How the platform runs the cluster, for example "appliance".
- `kube_config` (String, Sensitive) The cluster's admin kubeconfig file (YAML), for kubectl. It holds a long-lived cluster-admin credential: treat it, and the Terraform state that stores it, like a password. It is downloaded once the cluster is running (which needs a write API key), and again when the state holds none or the API server's address (endpoint, public_ip or public_port) changed.
- `kubernetes_version` (String) The Kubernetes version the cluster runs, for example "1.31.2".
- `network_id` (String) Id of the VPC network the nodes are in. Null in a standard zone.
- `node` (Attributes) Size of every node, from node_plan. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node))
- `node_health` (String) What Kubernetes last reported of the nodes while the cluster runs: "healthy" (every node Ready), "degraded" (a node is NotReady, or fewer are Ready than the cluster should run) or "unknown" (the nodes could not be read in the last 15 minutes, for example a private endpoint whose agent is not connected). Read about every 5 minutes; null while the cluster is not running. A degraded cluster still reports observed_state "running".
- `node_plan_id` (String) Id of the plan every node uses.
- `nodes` (Number) control_nodes plus workers: the number of VMs billed.
- `nodes_checked_at` (String) When the nodes were last read, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second; null if never.
- `observed_state` (String) State of the cluster as the platform sees it, for example "running", "updating" while a scale or upgrade runs, or "stopped".
- `public_ip` (String) The public address the API server is reached on when endpoint_access is public or dual; null until it has one, and for private.
- `public_port` (Number) The public port the API server is reached on when endpoint_access is public or dual; null until it has one, and for private.
- `ready_nodes` (Number) Nodes Kubernetes reported Ready at nodes_checked_at; null when node_health is unknown or null.
- `updated_at` (String) When the cluster was last changed, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `volume_storage_gb` (Number) Storage, in GB, that the workloads' persistent volume claims use. It is billed with the nodes' disks, and changes as workloads create and delete volumes.

<a id="nestedatt--autoscaling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `autoscaling`

Required:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the autoscaler runs. false is the same as leaving autoscaling out, and then min_workers and max_workers must be omitted.

Optional:

- `max_workers` (Number) Most workers, min_workers to 10. Required when enabled. Credit and account limits are checked for this many.
- `min_workers` (Number) Fewest workers, 1 to 10. Required when enabled.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--node"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node`

Read-Only:

- `disk_gb` (Number) Disk, in GB.
- `memory_mb` (Number) Memory, in MB.
- `vcpu` (Number) Virtual CPUs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A Kubernetes cluster is imported by its id. node_plan cannot be read back:
# set it in the configuration, and the next apply records it without resizing
# the cluster. The kubeconfig is downloaded on the first refresh.
terraform import pantechdynamics_kubernetes_cluster.prod k8s_06ggex1abcdefghjkmnpqrstvw
```
